correctness.rationale: PASS: For independent isotropic great circles, the Gram correlation density is 1/(4pi sqrt(1+2xyz-x²-y²-z²)). The four antipodal cell-pair areas A_i are pi/2 plus or minus arcsin correlation terms, sum to 2pi; the Jacobian and exact D=4 prod_i sin(A_i/2) yield a symmetric joint area density. On A1=2pi-eta, A2..A4=eta*t1..t3, the expanded joint form is eta³/(64pi)g(t)[1-eta²(1+sum t_i²)/48+O(eta^4)] uniformly including simplex faces. Independent rational Dirichlet moment calculations give E[prod(1-T_i)]=4/21 and weighted E[sum T_i²]=29/55, hence one-cell probability epsilon^4/672[1-7epsilon²/330+O(epsilon^4)], multiplied by four disjoint symmetry classes gives epsilon^4/168. The normalized deficit has Beta(4,1) and t simplex density 21/(8pi)prod(1-t_i)/sqrt(prod t_i), with O(epsilon²) TV via uniform density ratio. Script verifies rational factors/Gram identity on finite samples only; limiting proof analytic.
residual_risks: Finite 1,500 Gram samples and 90,000 importance samples cannot certify asymptotics.
